mcq.s: At what average speed does the Earth revolve around the Sun?
mcq.x: The Earth's mean orbital velocity is about 29.8 km/sec, i.e. roughly 30 km/sec.

mcq.s: Which one of the following conditions is most relevant for the presence of life on Mars?
o: Occurrence of ice cap and frozen water
mcq.x: Polar ice caps and frozen (and subsurface) water make Mars the planet most discussed for possible life; its thin CO2 atmosphere, cold temperatures and lack of an ozone layer are unfavourable.

mcq.s: How long does Saturn take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
mcq.x: Saturn's orbital period is about 29.5 years (29.46 Earth years); Uranus takes about 84 years.

mcq.s: How long does Uranus take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
mcq.x: Uranus revolves around the Sun once in about 84 Earth years; Neptune takes about 165 years.

mcq.s: Which of the following latitudinal positions of a place is possible?
mcq.x: Latitudes run only from 0° at the Equator to 90° N or 90° S at the poles; 'East' and 'West' are used for longitudes.

mcq.s: A plane starts from 30° N latitude, 50° E longitude and lands at the diametrically opposite point of the Earth. Where will it land?
mcq.x: The antipode of (x° N, y° E) is (x° S, (180 − y)° W), so 30° N, 50° E → 30° S, 130° W.

mcq.s: If the difference of longitude between two places is 90°, what is the difference in their local times?
mcq.x: Each degree of longitude equals 4 minutes of time, so 90° × 4 = 360 minutes = 6 hours.

mcq.s: Which of the following happens in India when the Sun shines vertically over the Tropic of Capricorn?
o: High pressure develops over North-West India
Low pressure develops over North-West India
No change in pressure occurs over North-West India
mcq.x: In December the Sun is over the Tropic of Capricorn; north-west India becomes cold and a high-pressure area forms there, sending dry winds outward (the winter / north-east monsoon season).

mcq.s: On June 21 every year, which of the following latitude(s) experience(s) sunlight of more than 12 hours? 1. Equator 2. Tropic of Cancer 3. Tropic of Capricorn 4. Arctic Circle
mcq.x: At the June solstice the Northern Hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, so the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle get more than 12 hours of daylight; the Equator always has about 12 hours and the Tropic of Capricorn less.

why: vague dating options; answer not sure
